Snow-capped peaks rise on both walls of the curve, meeting overhead as an inverted alpine ridge, glaciers hanging downward from the far-side summits, meltwater arcing impossibly across the curved sky.
A forest canopy fills the near ground, and above it the land curves sharply upward, treetops becoming a vertical wall of green that bends into an overhead ceiling of inverted woodland.
The overhead band of the ring reflects in the lake below, doubling the inverted landscape — real terrain hanging above, its mirror image shimmering in the water, the world curling all around.
Night falls unevenly across the curve, the near ground dark while the overhead terrain still catches axial light, the inverted cities glowing bright against the shadowed interior sky above.
A plaza opens to the full ring view — ground rising on every side into walls of architecture that bend overhead, the far-side district hanging inverted and lit, encircling the viewer in city.
The world-curve reads as pure geometry from this angle, the sweep of terrain up the right wall, across the overhead arc, and back down the left forming a perfect luminous band.
Mist fills the lower bowl of the habitat while the overhead terrain rises clear above it, the inverted landscape floating on a white cloud floor, the ring curving through atmosphere and light.

The horizon lifts on both flanks, curving upward until farmland and forest arc clean overhead, the far city hanging inverted in the zenith, its lights scattered across the ceiling of the world like fallen stars.

Terrain sweeps up the left wall in a continuous green band, bends across the top of the frame as an upside-down river valley, and descends the right wall, closing the ring behind the viewer without a seam.

A sheer wall of terraced cropland rises beside the camera at a stomach-dropping angle, bending overhead into a ceiling of gold and green, the curvature so tight the far shore hangs only kilometers above.

The axial sun catches the overhead terrain full-on, blazing the inverted hillsides into a luminous band of white and amber that arcs from wall to wall directly above, while the near ground falls in shadow below.
